original_test_intent: Verify the designated physical x16 PCIe slot and expected endpoint are consistently visible in BIOS Setup, UEFI shell and Linux, with negotiated generation and lane width meeting the approved platform topology and no PCIe errors.
original_method: Bind chassis slot label through riser/root port/switch/retimer to endpoint BDF/serial; preserve baseline AER and logs; operator captures BIOS and UEFI `pci -i`; agent collects complete Linux `lspci -Dnnvvv` for the same endpoint plus bridge chain and kernel/AER state; compare capability versus negotiated speed/width under an understood idle/power state to the qualified topology without changing settings or retraining links.
manual_activity: An operator captures the exact endpoint in BIOS Setup and UEFI shell; an owner provides physical topology and interprets any environment naming differences.
required_inputs: Platform/SKU/BIOS and populated physical slot/riser/topology drawing
Expected endpoint PN/serial/device IDs and slot-to-root-port/switch/retimer/BDF mapping
Required PCIe generation and x16 lane width at each link segment plus allowed power-state behavior
Authorized Linux/SSH/pciutils and BIOS/UEFI console access
safety_requirements: Use read-only enumeration only and verify the target host
Preserve prior AER/kernel/SEL evidence rather than clearing logs
Do not equate a BDF or endpoint name with physical slot without the approved topology
Do not reset/retrain devices or change BIOS to correct a mismatch
Stop and preserve evidence on missing endpoint, bridge-chain mismatch, downgrade, AER or instability
agent_execution_scope: Validate exact endpoint and topology identifiers before collecting Linux evidence
Collect complete domain-qualified Linux endpoint, capability, status, bridge and AER information
Correlate operator BIOS/UEFI artifacts without claiming physical observation
Do not navigate firmware UI, modify links/settings, clear logs or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve slot/riser/root-port/switch/retimer/endpoint map and x16 generation oracle
Supply/capture BIOS and UEFI evidence for the same endpoint
Resolve cross-environment differences and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: After target/tool checks and confirmation, collect complete `lspci -Dnnvvv` plus read-only kernel/AER context for the bound endpoint; combine with operator BIOS Setup and UEFI `pci -i` artifacts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Trace one physical slot to a stable endpoint identity and compare its capability/negotiated link across firmware and OS evidence against the approved topology.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical-to-logical mapping, endpoint serial/device identity, complete verbose output, bridge chain, AER state and no-retrain boundary.

review_improvement: Restores the source's firmware/UEFI/OS coverage and makes x16 acceptance physical-slot- and topology-specific instead of trusting a flat enumeration list.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PCIe endpoint appearing in `lspci` does not establish which chassis slot it occupies or whether an x16 connector is wired and negotiating x16. Switches and retimers add multiple link segments, while BDFs can change. The review therefore binds stable endpoint identity to the physical topology and separately evaluates LnkCap and LnkSta on the relevant segments. BIOS/UEFI evidence is an essential independent surface, not a package blocker or substitutable Linux output.
